decisions.actorTrace: Authenticated swarm route passes server-issued context to runBuildPipeline. Existing terminal worker supplies its owner/run and fenced terminal evidence to buildOutcomeFromTerminalRun. recentRoutingOutcomes is a global service-role-loaded cache, so matching runId alone did not establish owner equality.
decisions.invariant: Only telemetry whose userId AND runId match the admitted terminal run may attach model evidence or attest verification. Existing generation/terminal RPC fence remains mandatory and unchanged.

evidence.scope: In-memory deterministic association only, not database or whole-caller acceptance
Real model_routing_outcomes and fenced build_outcomes persistence, owner positive and foreign-owner negative

remaining: Execute new actual database case at final source
Reconcile unchanged legacy retention/upsert callers separately
Do not equate this narrow fix with whole-factory certification

decisions.actorTrace: runBuildPipeline has two production callers, both authenticated swarm execute branches. New required context is the original server-issued context, not request JSON. Restored execution databaseProjectId is checked too. Logical run/repository workspace keys remain distinct from UUID database projects and rely on existing owner-scoped stores.
decisions.invariant: Before durable run admission or provider preparation, any supplied/restored database project UUID must belong to the issued actor. No foreign/missing project may create a run or trigger failure notifications.

evidence.scope: Actual HTTP and SDK transport against fixture, not actual RLS/database proof
Issued versus forged context, exact owner predicate, UUID and logical-key compatibility
Actual two-user project ownership, HTTP/SSE denial and unchanged run rows

remaining: Execute fixed HTTP regression and new actual database case
